title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models

target_networks.name: small GPT-style transformer written from scratch (algorithmic/NLP tasks; default 3 layers, width 64)
target_networks.params: median 166 for smallest 100%-accurate algorithmic models (Opus); about 190,000 for NLP

target_networks.name: hand-written visual feature network for fMRI encoding (865-line program, 9,996 features)
hand-written word-feature model for story-listening fMRI
hand-written audio feature network for ECoG encoding (3,852 features)

domain: neuroscience (fMRI, ECoG brain encoding); algorithmic tasks and NLP
tasks_benchmarks: 13 algorithmic tasks (addition, multiplication, GCD, edit distance, etc.)

headline_result.text: LLM agents wrote transformers that reach 100% hidden accuracy on all 26 Opus runs of 13 algorithmic tasks, and a hand-written visual encoding model beat all seven interpretable baselines on the held-out NSD dataset (ventral 0.317 vs 0.256) while trailing AlexNet in ventral cortex.
headline_result.quote: All 26 runs on algorithmic tasks reach 100% accuracy both on the visible set and the hidden set (Fig. 2a), often by implementing a known algorithm in the weights.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 2 runs per task per LLM (algorithmic/NLP); single search per brain dataset

key_claims.claim: On NLP tasks the written models are crude; iWSP reaches respectable accuracy on 3 of 4 datasets but fails on paraphrase.
key_claims.quote: on 3 of the 4 NLP datasets iWSP builds models that achieve respectable performance well above a naive majority baseline (it fails on the relatively difficult Paraphrase task).

key_claims.claim: The visual encoding model transfers to the unseen NSD dataset and beats all seven interpretable baselines, but trails pretrained AlexNet in ventral cortex.
key_claims.quote: Compared with pretrained AlexNet, iWSP matches black-box accuracy in early visual cortex while trailing in ventral visual cortex (0.391).

key_claims.claim: In language fMRI, a sudden jump in performance came from story-position features, which exposed a scan-timing confound in the dataset.
key_claims.quote: We find that the new features added at this step surprisingly do not encode a word’s semantic content, but rather only its position in the story.

key_claims.claim: For ECoG, the written audio features slightly underperform Whisper but add variance Whisper misses.
key_claims.quote: As a result, combining both in one ridge regression significantly improves on Whisper alone, raising performance from 0.070 to 0.075

key_claims.claim: Interpretability was tested by rebuilding models from a 200-word description; algorithmic rebuilds kept 100% accuracy and stayed far closer in size than a no-description control.
key_claims.quote: On algorithmic tasks, rebuilt models have 1.74 times the original’s parameters on a geometric mean, against 2,043 times for the control (Fig. A2b).

limitations_stated.text: Agents recombine known motifs (textbook algorithms, Gabor filters) rather than invent new computational principles.
limitations_stated.quote: First, current agents do not invent genuinely new computational principles.

limitations_stated.text: Programming deep hierarchical representations without backpropagation remains open, which likely explains trailing trained networks in ventral cortex, harder NLP and ECoG.
limitations_stated.quote: Programming deep hierarchical representations without backpropagation remains an open problem

limitations_stated.text: Training bans in the algorithmic harness are only instructions audited afterwards; some Sonnet runs fit weights to labels and were excluded.
limitations_stated.quote: The harness cannot stop the agent’s own Python from training or from computing the answer outside the network, so those rules remain instructions that we audit afterward.

notes_for_review: Extends WSP from editing to writing small interpretable networks from scratch with an evaluator-feedback loop, with brain-encoding feature extractors as the main scientific use (ridge regression is fitted on top of the hand-written features). Evidence is fairly careful: hidden sets, held-out subjects/datasets, classical and black-box baselines, audits for hidden training, and a text-bottleneck rebuild test with a no-description control. Written models still trail pretrained networks where deep hierarchies matter, and total API cost was about $17,500. It does not touch MIT's Qwen math edit.
